messages:
maria_support: Customer hit a sudden spike of 502 / TLS handshake failures after migrating traffic to a VPCE (interface). Endpoint: vpce-0a1b2c3d. Affected clients in their prod VPC. Any quick checks?
kevin_infra: Can you paste a minimal curl -v and what api hostname they resolve to from the client VPC? Also curious if they toggled Private DNS on the endpoint.
maria_support: Sure — from one affected instance: ```$ host api.redwood.com
api.redwood.com has address 10.12.5.23
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.com/health
*   Trying 10.12.5.23...
* Connected to api.redwood.com (10.12.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* error:14094410:SSL routines:SSL3_READ_BYTES:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
} ``` They also reported some clients see "SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'api.redwood.com'" intermittently.
liam_eng: That sounds like an SNI / cert hostname mismatch. What does the server cert present? Can you run `openssl s_client -connect 10.12.5.23:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts` and paste subject/SAN?
maria_support: Customer ran that: ```CONNECTED(00000003)
subject=/CN=redwood-api.internal
issuer=/CN=ACME Internal CA
subjectAltName=DNS:redwood-internal, DNS:api.internal
---
no peer certificate available or cert missing expected SAN 'api.redwood.com'
``` So cert has internal names only.
kevin_infra: Two likely root causes: (A) ALB in front of the service is terminating TLS and presenting an internal cert (ALB listener configured with internal cert), or (B) traffic is being TCP-proxied to a backend that serves internal certs. Which type of endpoint did they create? interface VPCE -> ALB (HTTPS) or NLB (TCP)?
jess_oncall: Quick checklist: 1) If they use ALB (HTTPS) the ALB must present a cert that includes api.redwood.com. 2) If they want to keep backend internal certs, use NLB passthrough and terminate at the backend with SNI matched cert. 3) Ensure Private DNS is enabled so api.redwood.com resolves to the VPCE IP in the client VPC (otherwise clients may still resolve to public IPs and the TLS SNI/public certs mismatch). Also check SG / NACL for ephemeral port egress. Quick repro command I recommend customers run from an instance: ```host api.redwood.com && curl -v --resolve 'api.redwood.com:443:10.12.5.23' https://api.redwood.com/health```
maria_support: They said Private DNS was enabled on the VPCE, but they still saw failures only from instances in a specific subnet behind a NAT. I did a traceroute from that instance: ```traceroute to api.redwood.com (10.12.5.23), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.2.1 (10.0.2.1)  0.2 ms 0.1 ms 0.1 ms
 2  10.0.1.1 (10.0.1.1)  1.0 ms 1.1 ms 1.0 ms
 3  52.95.1.9 (52.95.1.9)  10.2 ms 10.1 ms 10.2 ms
``` That looks like DNS queries from the subnet are being forwarded out to the internet/NAT, not to the VPC-resolver -> resulted in hitting a public edge and getting a different cert.
kevin_infra: If instances use a custom DNS (bind/unbound or a DNS forwarder) that forwards unknown names to 8.8.8.8 or the IGW, Route53 Private DNS won't be applied. Two fixes: (a) point the resolver to AmazonProvidedDNS (VPC resolver at .2) or (b) create an inbound Route53 resolver endpoint and conditional forwarding for their custom DNS. Also verify DHCP option set isn't overriding DNS server to the NAT.
liam_eng: Also check the endpoint's ENI SG allows inbound 443 from the client instances (or their SG), and that the ALB's target group health checks originate from the VPCE IP ranges — sometimes health checks fail and route traffic to wrong backend which returns internal cert/redirects. If the ALB listener is redirecting to /login, that can turn API calls into 302 -> client fails.
maria_support: Customer confirmed: they were using an ALB with a cert for api.redwood.com but had a redirect rule for unauthenticated hosts which kicked in when Host header was rewritten by a proxy. They also had a DNS forwarder on one subnet configured to 10.0.0.5 which forwards to 8.8.8.8. So queries for api.redwood.com from that subnet resolved to public IPs instead of the VPCE IP.
jess_oncall: Recommended remediation we gave them: 1) Fix DNS path: point the forwarder to AmazonProvidedDNS or add Route53 inbound endpoints and conditional forwarding for VPC private zone; 2) If they want TLS passthrough, switch VPCE target to an NLB (TCP) so SNI is preserved and backend certs are accepted; 3) If staying with ALB, ensure ALB listener presents cert containing api.redwood.com and remove redirect rules for API host; 4) Confirm SGs allow ephemeral port ranges and that NACLs aren't blocking return traffic.
maria_support: Customer will try switching the subnet forwarder to .2 (AmazonProvidedDNS) and, as a backup, create an inbound resolver. They will also change ALB listener to present the public cert and remove the redirect. They said they'll post results. Thanks. :thumbsup:
vpce-bot: Ticket 12345 updated: escalated to infra; note added "client-subnet-forwarder-causing-public-dns-resolve"
